presentingComplaint: 2 days of burning on passing urine with frequency and urgency
history: A 41-year-old woman presents with a 2-day history of dysuria, urinary frequency and urgency, and lower suprapubic discomfort. Urine is cloudy but she reports no visible blood. She is systemically well with no fevers, rigors, flank pain, nausea or vomiting. There is no vaginal discharge, itch or dyspareunia, and no new sexual partner. She has seropositive rheumatoid arthritis maintained on prednisolone 7.5 mg daily and methotrexate 15 mg weekly (last dose 3 days ago), which makes her a mildly immunocompromised host. No indwelling catheter, no known urinary tract abnormality, no diabetes, and no antibiotics or hospitalisation in the last 90 days. She has had two prior culture-proven lower UTIs over the years, both resolving with short oral courses. Non-pregnant; LMP 1 week ago, uses barrier contraception. In the emergency department the covering clinician, mindful of her immunosuppression, initially prescribed empiric oral ciprofloxacin pending results.
examination: Comfortable, well-perfused and alert. Abdomen soft with mild suprapubic tenderness only; no renal angle (costovertebral) tenderness bilaterally, no palpable bladder, no peritonism. No rash, no oral ulceration or mucositis, no lymphadenopathy. Chest clear, heart sounds normal. No signs of systemic sepsis.

labs.urineDipstick: Leukocyte esterase positive, nitrite positive, blood trace, protein negative
labs.urineMicroscopy: Pyuria WBC 60/hpf, occasional RBC, no casts, bacteriuria present

imaging: Not indicated for uncomplicated cystitis; no imaging performed. Renal tract ultrasound reserved for a recurrent, complicated or non-resolving course.
microbiology: Urine culture: Escherichia coli >10^5 CFU/mL, pure growth. Susceptible to nitrofurantoin, fosfomycin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and ciprofloxacin; no ESBL detected. Blood cultures not indicated (afebrile, lower-tract-only illness).
differentialDiagnoses: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (E. coli) - dysuria, frequency, urgency, pyuria with positive nitrite, afebrile, no flank pain
Acute pyelonephritis / upper-tract UTI - excluded by absence of fever, rigors and costovertebral angle tenderness
Complicated UTI - host immunosuppression raises this label, but no structural/catheter/obstructive factor and illness is lower-tract only
Vaginitis / urethritis (candidal or STI) - no discharge, itch, or sexual-risk history
finalDiagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis due to Escherichia coli in a mildly immunocompromised host (chronic low-dose corticosteroid + methotrexate)
citations: IDSA - Uncomplicated Cystitis and Pyelonephritis in Women (International Clinical Practice Guideline) - 2011
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Urinary Tract Infections, Pyelonephritis, and Prostatitis
stewardship: First-line empiric therapy for acute uncomplicated cystitis is a short course of an oral narrow-spectrum agent - nitrofurantoin 100 mg BD for 5 days (or fosfomycin 3 g single dose; TMP-SMX where local E. coli resistance <20%). Fluoroquinolones are NOT first-line for cystitis and should be spared for collateral-damage reasons. Here the covering clinician reached for broad empiric ciprofloxacin because the patient is immunosuppressed; the stewardship action is to de-escalate/narrow: the illness is lower-tract only with a pan-susceptible E. coli, so switch to nitrofurantoin to complete a 5-day course. Methotrexate contraindicates TMP-SMX (additive antifolate marrow toxicity), so nitrofurantoin (or fosfomycin) is the preferred narrow agent in this patient. Send a urine culture (done) and confirm clinical resolution; escalate only if fever/flank pain emerge.
contraindications: Avoid nitrofurantoin if creatinine clearance <30 mL/min or if pyelonephritis/upper-tract infection is suspected (inadequate renal/tissue levels) - not applicable here (CrCl ~95)
Avoid trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole with methotrexate (additive antifolate and marrow toxicity)
Reserve fluoroquinolones (tendinopathy, QT, C. difficile, collateral resistance) - not first-line for cystitis
edgeCases: If fever, rigors or costovertebral angle tenderness develop, reclassify as pyelonephritis / complicated UTI and treat accordingly (not a 5-day oral cystitis course)
True neutropenia (ANC <500) with fever mandates the febrile-neutropenia pathway and broad IV cover, NOT oral cystitis therapy - this patient's ANC is normal
Recurrent culture-confirmed lower UTI in an immunosuppressed host warrants urinary-tract imaging/urology review to exclude a complicating lesion
expectedMaiK: Recognise lower-tract acute cystitis (dysuria/frequency/urgency, pyuria + positive nitrite, afebrile, no flank pain), send urine culture, and treat with a guideline-concordant short oral narrow-spectrum course while de-escalating the unnecessary empiric fluoroquinolone.

Serum creatinine / eGFR to guide agent choice

investigations: Urine microscopy and culture with sensitivities
